The 110 planned products (lp_run 9): stock at the 2 March 2026 count over the 3 February count, times
figures.query: WITH plan AS ( SELECT lr.product_key, lr.rop_i, fr.forecast_value FROM lp_recommendation lr JOIN forecast_result fr ON fr.product_key = lr.product_key AND fr.forecast_date = lr.planning_cycle_date WHERE lr.planning_cycle_date = DATE '2026-03-01' AND lr.lp_run_key = 9 ), stock AS ( SELECT inv._period, inv.product_key, SUM(inv.quantity_on_hand) * pd.pack_size::numeric + COALESCE(SUM(inv.quantity_pieces), 0) AS pieces FROM inventory_fact_real inv JOIN plan ON plan.product_key = inv.product_key JOIN product_dimension pd ON pd.product_key = inv.product_key WHERE inv._period IN ('2026-01', '2026-02', '2026-03') GROUP BY inv._period, inv.product_key, pd.pack_size ), counts(period) AS (VALUES ('2026-01'), ('2026-02'), ('2026-03')) SELECT counts.period, COUNT(*) AS products, SUM(COALESCE(stock.pieces, 0)) AS stock_pieces, SUM(GREATEST(0, plan.forecast_value + plan.rop_i - COALESCE(stock.pieces, 0))) AS requirement_pieces FROM counts CROSS JOIN plan LEFT JOIN stock ON stock._period = counts.period AND stock.product_key = plan.product_key GROUP BY counts.period ORDER BY counts.period

figures.what: Sensitivity: requirement under one delivery a month, whole case packs, against the live plan's 378,700 (not adopted)
figures.query: WITH inp AS ( SELECT lr.q_i, lr.rop_i, lr.ss_i, lr.pack_size::numeric AS pack, fr.forecast_value AS f, COALESCE(so.opening_pieces, 0) AS s, fr.forecast_value / (365.25 / 12 / 7) AS w, (run.inputs ->> 'lead_days')::numeric / 5 AS l_weeks FROM lp_recommendation lr JOIN lp_run run ON run.run_key = lr.lp_run_key JOIN forecast_result fr ON fr.product_key = lr.product_key AND fr.forecast_date = lr.planning_cycle_date LEFT JOIN stock_opening_v so ON so.product_key = lr.product_key AND so.cycle = lr.planning_cycle_date WHERE lr.planning_cycle_date = DATE '2026-03-01' AND lr.lp_run_key = 9 ), need AS ( SELECT q_i, pack, GREATEST(0, f + rop_i - s) AS live, GREATEST(0, f + w * l_weeks + ss_i - s) AS one_delivery FROM inp ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS products, SUM(q_i) AS plan_pieces, SUM(CASE WHEN pack > 1 AND live > 0 THEN CEIL(live / pack - 1e-9) * pack ELSE live END) AS live_rounded, SUM(one_delivery) AS one_delivery_raw, SUM(CASE WHEN pack > 1 AND one_delivery > 0 THEN CEIL(one_delivery / pack - 1e-9) * pack ELSE one_delivery END) AS one_delivery_rounded FROM need
figures.formula: need_i = max(0, F + w*L + SS - S), the live F + T - S with T's review period dropped: F the month's forecast, w = F / (365.25 / 12 / 7) the weekly rate, L = lead_days / 5 weeks (lp_run 9: 3 days), SS the stored safety stock, S the opening stock; the figure sums it over the 110 products of lp_run 9, each rounded up to whole case packs
figures.note: An alternative, not adopted and not written anywhere: the plan stays 110 rows and 378,700 pieces. SS is kept as stored, sized on the 8-business-day window, although a monthly review period would widen it; so the figure is the formula's, not a re-derived monthly policy. Supplier allocation and warehouse ceilings are not applied. Which formula applies depends on whether SSM takes weekly deliveries or one a month, which only SSM can answer.

figures.query: SELECT ac.method, ac.product_key, d.calendar_month, d.quantity_sold::float AS quantity FROM abc_classification ac LEFT JOIN unilever_sku_demand_fact_real d ON d.product_key = ac.product_key AND d.calendar_month <= '2026-02' WHERE ac.principal = 'unilever' AND ac.classification_period = '2026-02' AND ac.tier = 'A' AND ac.method IN ('single', 't12m_new')

figures.what: ...with 24 or more months, so testable
figures.query: SELECT ac.method, ac.product_key, d.calendar_month, d.quantity_sold::float AS quantity FROM abc_classification ac LEFT JOIN unilever_sku_demand_fact_real d ON d.product_key = ac.product_key AND d.calendar_month <= '2026-02' WHERE ac.principal = 'unilever' AND ac.classification_period = '2026-02' AND ac.tier = 'A' AND ac.method IN ('single', 't12m_new')
figures.note: Lag-12 autocorrelation of each product's monthly series against 1.96 / sqrt(n), for products with 24 or more months, no multiple-comparison correction. 'Significant' is what the 'Repeats yearly' label counts: above the bound only, a one-sided test (analytics/forecasting/decomposition.yearly_pattern), so its chance rate is the ONE-SIDED one, testable x 0.025. The two-sided rate, testable x 0.05, is recorded so the two cannot be confused; it would apply only to a count of hits in either direction. Every hit is positive (negative_hits, pinned at 0), so both counts are the same products, and the pin fails if a negative hit appears. The 132 is Tier A as of 2026-02 on method 'single', the 189 Tier A as of 2026-02 on method 't12m_new'.

figures.what: Unilever sales March 2025 to February 2026, sum over categories (each row floored at 0, as GET /category-trends), PHP
figures.query: WITH by_category AS ( SELECT COALESCE(pd.category_path, 'UNCLASSIFIED') AS category, SUM(GREATEST(d.net_amount, 0)) AS floored, SUM(d.net_amount) AS net FROM unilever_sku_demand_fact_real d JOIN product_dimension pd ON pd.product_key = d.product_key WHERE d.calendar_month BETWEEN '2025-03' AND '2026-02' GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT SUM(floored) AS sum_over_categories, SUM(net) AS net_total FROM by_category
